training_note: Use ham as legitimate negatives only after the official file is verified; never use UCI 'spam' as scam positives.
schema: canonical msg-v1 (see docs/REAL_DATA_STRATEGY.md); raw columns listed in 'raw_columns'

label_schema.canonical: ham -> legit; spam -> spam (NOT scam: mixes premium-rate prize scams and marketing)

paper: Almeida, Gómez Hidalgo, Yamakami. Contributions to the Study of SMS Spam Filtering. DocEng 2011
pii_status: unmasked; phone numbers and short codes in text
collection_method: UK spam reports from Grumbletext + ham sampled from NUS SMS Corpus and a PhD thesis corpus; manual labels
limitations: Ham overlaps the NUS SMS Corpus
Contained (87.6%) in Super SMS and (~85%) in Mishra & Soni: never mix those with UCI across splits
provenance: Official file from UCI (local download). The GitHub copy is used only for the leakage audit.
name: SMS Spam Collection v.1
source: Almeida & Gómez Hidalgo (UCI Machine Learning Repository)
license: CC-BY-4.0 (stated on the UCI page; not verified from here because UCI is blocked)
original_or_mirror: official via local download; GitHub copy is third-party

fetch.instructions: Download smsspamcollection.zip from the official URL, unzip, then: python scripts/fetch_real_datasets.py register uci_sms_spam --from <unzipped folder> --pin
